dedupe_keys.name: kathmandu valley single hazards and multi hazard interrelationships database

description: Thompson and colleagues deposit an Excel database of hazards and their interactions for Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. Zenodo lists a public workbook under CC BY 4.0. The provider reports evidence from 58 sources for single hazards and 21 for multi-hazard links, identifies 21 hazard types and 83 interrelationships, and says twelve links have direct evidence of past influence in the valley. Named sheets hold single-hazard evidence, relationship evidence, an interaction matrix, definitions and references. The source types include academic and grey literature, media, databases and social media. Modellers could use this matrix to choose plausible hazard sequences and stress tests for infrastructure cascading-failure or emergency-response simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this Kathmandu evidence matrix. A limitation is that an evidenced relationship is not a quantified transition probability or damage function. Only twelve links have direct local case evidence, and the compilation may miss events outside the searched material. The workbook was not downloaded; individual citations and matrix coding were not independently checked.
